correctness.rationale: The exact de Bruijn sum is derived from the known Rees correspondence and factor-upset closure, including precise multiplicity of loops. Each remainder range has an explicit uniform bound for fixed k, and the standalone exact enumerator checks six small parameter pairs plus seven independent two-vertex histograms. Enumeration is not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The correspondence between congruences and multiplicative ideals is explicitly previously known (Gao–Zhou, lines 44–50) and is NOT the claimed original contribution. The new claimed implication is the explicit de Bruijn two-arc coefficient Q_k(n) with all-fixed-k exponentially small third-order error and independent k=2 exact identity. Gao–Zhou and Gao–Ren–Zhao develop identity-basis characterizations and do not give these coefficients; Bailey–Finn-Sell–Snocken study index growth for an infinite free semigroup rather than this fixed-truncation, alphabet-growth regime. Targeted scientific literature and mathematical-record comparisons found no comparable implication. value.rationale: This determines the first three asymptotic orders of a canonical congruence-count invariant for every fixed nilpotency cutoff, including the exact rare-collapse mechanism and a combinatorially informative de Bruijn overlap correction. Such numerical structure is not supplied by the known congruence–ideal correspondence, by a single finite census, or by finite-basis theorems. The bound is sharp at the level of the displayed coefficients and isolates a natural new structural statistic.
